title: Mirror permutation-orbit audit
hypothesis: For a trained one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP, hidden-unit permutation Views with correspondingly permuted incoming weights/biases and outgoing rows will preserve test outputs to numerical tolerance. Encoding 8 such Views as base weights plus paid permutation indices may appear to compress compared with 8 checkpoint copies, but permutation count must not be called functional multiplicity if outputs do not change.
mirror_coordinate: hidden-unit permutation indices applied consistently across adjacent tensors
logical_multiplicity: eight parameter coordinate variants in one exact function orbit
controls: one shared checkpoint plus eight paid permutation index vectors
permutation applied only to incoming weights as a negative control

development.selection_metric: maximum and RMS output difference on held-out examples and actual serialized bytes

storage.authority: actual deterministic fixed-timestamp ZIP/NPY FP16 payload bytes

success_gate: Audit confirms functional equivalence within max abs output difference <=1e-5 after FP16 reload in all fresh seeds; quantify actual bytes and explicitly classify the orbit as zero additional function multiplicity.
failure_gate: Consistent function difference >1e-5 after correct permutation of all symmetry-coupled tensors, indicating a broken symmetry implementation or numerical issue requiring NOT ESTABLISHED.
boundaries: permutation orbit is a symmetry audit, not a compression win
permutations are parameter-coordinate variants of one function
only a single synthetic trained MLP is evaluated
sign/scale symmetries and other architectures are not tested
